lines: Word came up from the Hall before you did.
The road east is easier than the road in was. Everything is.
Down off the pass, then. Tideglass water still in your boots, by the look.
Everything you can see is here because the ground is hot. The rest of it came over that mountain on a cart.
Down off the pass. Mind the last stretch — that is cinder, and cinder moves.
Everything you can see is here because the ground is hot. The rest of it came over that mountain on a cart.
Two hundred and eleven carts this month, and eleven I logged as EQUIPMENT without opening.
The seal said Foundation. I have started copying those pages out.
I do not know who for yet. I will know when they ask.
Two hundred and eleven carts this month. Charcoal, ore, charcoal, ore.
And eleven I logged as EQUIPMENT and did not open, because the seal said Foundation.

ef_pan_walker: I walk the water down. Four pans, one into the next, and it loses a little heat in each.
Straight off the rock it would strip the copper out of a main in a season.
My mother did this. Her mother did this. The pans are older than either of them.
ef_spring_keeper: The springs do not run because we are lucky. They run because something under us is breathing.
My grandfather said that, and he said it politely, in case it was listening.
ef_bather: An hour in the Steepings and my hands stop shaking.
Ask any smith in Caelora what that is worth. Then ask one who is fifty.
ef_pipefitter: Every main starts at the pans and runs downhill. No pumps. Never had one, never needed one.
There is a stretch under the market that is older than the market. Older than the city, if you push me.
ef_pipe_apprentice: I can tell what is in a pipe by hitting it.
Water sings. Steam knocks. Nothing at all just hurts your hand.
ef_lamp_tapper: Nobody in Emberfall has ever bought lamp oil. The lamps are tapped straight off the mains.
When the pipes go cold the city goes dark. It has happened twice — once for an hour, once for nine days.

lines: FLAME HALL SITS FROM SECOND BELL — oh. It is you.
I have been shouting your name since noon and you walked past me twice.
FLAME HALL SITS FROM SECOND BELL. THE KEEPER TAKES ALL COMERS.
AND FINISHES MOST OF THEM BEFORE THIRD.

ef_challenger: Third attempt. First time I brought Tide types, which was clever of me right up until it was not.
You do not out-think a Flame Hall in a town where the floor is warm.
ef_hall_child: There is a crack in the square that goes down forever.
Dad says it goes down about six feet. Dad has not looked.
ef_clinic_queue: Burns, mostly. Sometimes the kin, sometimes the trainer, usually both.
The keeper does not charge. She also does not lecture, which is the rarer thing.
ef_market_carter: Copper out, charcoal in. That is this whole city in four words.
We send bands and pipe collars as far as Skyreach. There is a Hall up on those cliffs roofed in our sheet.
ef_ash_sweeper: Twice a month the mountain clears its throat and I have a week of work.
You get used to the sweeping. You do not get used to the taste.
ef_smith_wife: He comes home the colour of the road and sleeps like the dead. Forty years of it.
I would not swap it. There is nowhere in Caelora warm like a forge town in winter.
ef_street_kid: A boy came through on his own, two days back. Green coat, would not stop talking.
He asked me who signs for the Foundation carts. I said nobody signs, they just go.
He wrote that down. Nobody writes down what I say.
ef_tenement_elder: Four floors, eleven families, one stove between the lot of us, and nobody is cold.
Try that in Stonewake. Try that anywhere.
ef_foundry_foreman: The foundry has not gone out in a hundred and forty years. Not once, not for a day.
If it ever did, the ground would not relight it. We would be carting fire over the pass like everybody else.
ef_forge_master: Three mouths under one roof and three masters who do not speak to each other. It works.
You want a vessel band, go to Hesk at the end of the row. He is better than me and I will deny saying it.
ef_charcoal_carter: Nothing grows in a caldera. Every stick of charcoal in this city climbed a mountain to get here.
So copper is dear and heat is free. Backwards, is it not.
ef_slag_child: It is warm the whole way through. You can sit on it in the rain.
You cannot sit on the shiny bits. I only did that once.

lines: They say the one up in the pass opened. For you.
Then this one is the same door, and I have been standing in front of the wrong end of it for thirty years.
The old gate. Nobody has had it open in living memory, and people have tried with hammers.
There is a hollow cut in the middle of it, about the size of your hand.
There is another door like it somewhere up the pass. Nobody has had that one open either.

ef_causeway_elder: The road stops at the kerb because the ground past the kerb will not hold one.
They laid it four times. Now they lay it once and leave the rest to the cracks.
It only ever went to the gate anyway, and the gate has never gone anywhere.
ef_fissure_surveyor: Foundation survey. We are mapping the fissures — they creep about a foot a year, north-north-east.
Towards the old gate, since you ask. Nobody has asked.

lines: Foundation business. You have that look people get in Tideglass.
Whatever you were told down there, up here we survey rock. That is all I am paid to know.
Foundation business. Geothermal research, if you want the words for it.
You would be amazed what a city like this leaves lying about, once you have bought the freight schedule.

ef_east_road_hand: I guide the east road. Or I did, until the shoulder came down on it in the spring.
Past that fall it goes down, and then it goes wet. Two days to Mirehaven if you keep your boots dry.
Nobody has ever kept their boots dry.
ef_inn_barker: The Cinder Rest. Warm floor, hot water, and a singer who will not stop for anything.
Rooms are short this month. The Foundation took six and I have seen two of them used.
ef_offduty_smith: Off shift. Do not ask me to look at anything.
